#            "fork deleted / upstream modified".

# Columns: hunks <TAB> status <TAB> path <TAB> disposition
#   status: UU = both modified, DU = deleted by fork / modified upstream,
#           UD = deleted by upstream / modified by fork
#
# Disposition keys:
#   keep-deletion   fork intentionally removed the file; keep the removal
#   take-deletion   upstream intentionally removed the file and the fork's edit is
#                   moot; take upstream's deletion
#   keep-fork       keep fork's side, in its own labelled block
#   merge           both sides' changes are carried, in the order noted
#   merge-docs      ordinary documentation merge, no code impact (re-apply branding)
#   seam:<module>   handled by the module's seam; the seam spec is authoritative
#   retarget        fork test the merge silently re-pointed at upstream's split
#                   modules; keep the fork's stack as the assertion target (3.10)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Deliberate removals (task 9.7, decision D9) — re-decide on every sync
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# These five files are `DU`: the fork deleted them while upstream modified
# them. "Keep our deletion" is a standing decision, so it is written down
# rather than re-derived. scripts/sync_report.py prints this list on every
# conflicted sync so an operator re-confirms it instead of re-applying it.
#
# README.md, docs/zh/README.md, docs/zh/README-Hant.md, docs/ja/README.md
#   The fork ships no READMEs at all (upstream 25 -> fork 0): the product name,
#   install story and screenshots in upstream's READMEs describe a different
#   build. Upstream edits to them are therefore *not* carried across; the
#   fork's user-facing docs live in doc/ and webhelp/. Re-decide if the fork
#   ever needs an upstream-style README (then take upstream's file and edit it,
#   do not resurrect the deletion). The 2026-09-19 sync found two more of these
#   (channel/web/README.md, channel/web/static/vendor/README.md) and kept the
#   deletion for both: the first describes upstream's entry module, which this
#   fork's D8 entry module deliberately is not.
#
# desktop/src/renderer/src/components/PermissionSelector.tsx
#   Replaced by the RBAC execution-permission model (permission set comes from
#   the tenant role and its resource grants, not a local selector).
#   tests/test_execution_permission_ui.cjs asserts the component and its toggle
#   are absent, so re-adding one would fail that test rather than silently
#   reintroduce a second authorization path. Re-decide if the desktop client
#   ever needs to *display* (not choose) effective permissions.
#
# `desktop/build/notarize-dmg.sh` is the mirror image (`UD`, upstream deleted):
# it is dispositioned `take-deletion`, *not* `keep-deletion`, so it is
# deliberately **not** in DELIBERATE_REMOVALS — the fork holds no standing
# decision to remove that file, upstream just retired it.
#
# `scripts/sync_report.py::DELIBERATE_REMOVALS` stays at the original five names
# (task 4.9 re-confirms them on every sync). The two README deletions the
# 2026-09-19 sync added are therefore reported by that script with a
# "(not in DELIBERATE_REMOVALS)" note: that is the intended signal, and the
# decision behind them is the README decision narrated above, not a new one.
